answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to lock a refundable bond in a shared kernel of trust before it may trade. The bond is small for one honest agent but multiplies with each new identity, so a fake fleet pays a fortune upfront. Random peer audits then mirror real work: auditors sample an agent's recent trades and demand proof it actually did the job. An identity caught faking loses its bond and its history, so the voyage from newcomer to trusted trader takes time and money no attacker can cheaply fake at scale.
